title: PUBLIC HEARING TONIGHT
full_story:
The City of Flora will be having a public meeting tonight before the regularly scheduled City Council meeting.

The public meeting is at 4:15 pm and is to afford citizens the opportunity to provide oral or written comments concerning the Community Development Block Grant Program (CDBG) fund public infrastructure grant.  The grant was used to reline sanitary sewer lines, line manholes and related costs in a targeted area in the City of Flora.

Those attending the public hearing will be provided with information including but not limited to: (1) project and grant costs, (2) time schedules, (3) project outcomes, (4) completed scope of work.  The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) was a request for monies to finance public infrastructure costs related to the construction of a targeted sewer main improvements project and related costs located in the City of Flora.

The public meeting is tonight at 4:15 at the Flora City Hall, everyone is welcome.

title: MILES OF SMILES
full_story:
Miles of Smiles will be at the Clay City School District on Wednesday and at the North Clay School District on March 10th, 11th and 12th.  Miles of Smiles Ltd. is providing preventative dental services at both districts to eligible children in all grades.

Services may include an exam/screening by a licensed dentist or licensed and certified public health dental hygienist, a cleaning fluoride varnish application, and sealant placement if needed.  This also satisfies the dental requirement mandated by the State of Illinois for school children for Kindergarten 2nd, 6th, and 9th grades.  There is no cost to the family or the school district.  After the services are performed, the following entities will be billed where applicable: IL Medicaid Program, public/private grants, or private dental insurance.

Miles of Smiles Ltd. will accept any reimbursement as the final payment, even if the claim is denied.  The families and the schools are never billed for any copayments, deductibles, or balances.

Consent forms can be returned to the Clay City school nurse Ms. Withrow or you may register your student online by scanning the QR code on the Miles of Smiles forms.  Please contact Ms. Withrow at [email protected] if you have any questions or concerns. For more information for Miles of Smiles at North Clay call 309-382-6405 or call the school at 618-665-3101.

title: DAYLIGHT SAVINGS TIME
full_story:
Whether digital or analog, Illinoisans will set their clocks forward Saturday night as daylight saving time returns.

Despite years of debate in Congress about ending the twice-yearly clock change, daylight saving time remains in place for 2026.  That means most of the US, will “spring forward” on March 8th.

Most smartphones, computers and other connected devices will update automatically.  But people will need to manually change non-smart devices such as microwaves, older car radios and analog wall clocks.

Efforts to eliminate the biannual clock change have stalled at both the federal and state levels.

In 2022, the US Senate unanimously passed the Sunshine Protection Act, which would have made daylight saving time permanent.  The House did not take it up.  The bill resurfaced in Congress in 2025 but again failed to advance.

President Donald Trump has voiced support for ending the clock changes.  In December 2024, then-president-elect Trump said he wanted to eliminate daylight saving time and move to year-round standard time.  He reiterated that stance in April 2025.

Until Congress passes legislation and a president signs it into law, the clock changes will continue nationwide.

Clocks will move back one hour, giving most Americans an extra hour of sleep on November 1st.

title: FLORA PRE K SCREENING
full_story:
Parents of all 3 year and 4-year-old children residing in Flora Community Unit School District are invited to bring their children to the district’s pre-k screening.  If your child is currently enrolled as a preschool student or has previously been screened you DO NOT need to have another screening.

The screenings will be held on March 18th, 19th, and 20th at the First Christian Church, located on the corner of North Main and West 4th Street.

Parents should make an appointment by going to the Flora School website to complete the Pre-K Screening Form, and you will be contacted with a screening time for your child.  If you have any questions, call 618-662-2014 and ask for Bristol Burroughs.

Pre-K Students must have family income documentation on file in order to determine eligibility for the program.  Parents should bring income information, certified birth certificate, immunization record, lead screening result, Social Security Number, and school physical for their child to be in the Pre-K Program.

The Flora Unit # 35 P.A.T Prevention Initiative will be offering free developmental screenings for children ages birth to three during the Flora Pre-K Screenings.  Early detection of developmental delays will benefit a child for a lifetime.  If you are interested, please call 618-662-2014 and ask for Bristol Burroughs to make an appointment.

title: IECC SPIN NIGHTS
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges (IECC) will host a series of Student/Parent Information Nights, known as SPIN Nights, to help prospective students and their families take the next step toward college enrollment.

Each campus will host its own SPIN Night from 5:30 to 7 pm on the following dates, at Frontier Community College tomorrow, at Olney Central College on Thursday, at Lincoln Trail College on March 19th, and at Wabash Valley College at March 17th.

SPIN Night is designed as a one-stop opportunity for students and parents to explore IECC programs, connect with key staff members, and learn more about the enrollment process.

During the event, attendees can explore academic programs, speak with Financial Aid representatives, schedule advising appointments, learn about student clubs and organizations, and discover support services available through each campus’s Learning Commons.

“SPIN Night is about making college planning simple and approachable for both students and their families,” said Carrie Halbert, IECC Director of Student Engagement and Recruitment.  “We want them to walk in with questions and leave feeling confident about their next steps.”

Halbert said the event allows families to gather information in one setting rather than trying to piece together details on their own.

“Students can meet advisors, talk through financial aid options, and see the support systems we have in place,” Halbert said.  “It’s an opportunity to see firsthand how IECC helps students succeed from day one.”

Registration is encouraged.  Students and parents can scan the QR code included on promotional materials to select the campus and date they plan to attend.

In addition to SPIN Night activities, Lincoln Trail College will also host an Ag Exploration Night on March 19th, giving attendees the opportunity to learn more about agricultural programs and careers.

For more information about SPIN Nights and to register, visit iecc.edu/spin or scan the QR code on event materials.

title: OLNEY MAN SENTENCED
full_story:
A district judge sentenced an Olney man to 28 years in federal prison after he admitted to producing child pornography of a 13-year-old minor.

Joseph Jared St. Pierre, 37, pleaded guilty to one count of production of child pornography.  Upon release from prison, he will serve 15 years of supervised release.

“Repeated sexual acts against minors is reprehensible, and the Justice Department will relentlessly pursue offenders who prey on and exploit children,” said US Attorney Steven D. Weinhoeft.

According to court documents, law enforcement officers responded to a report of sexual assault in July 2024 when the mother of a 13-year-old minor discovered a video on the minor’s cell phone of the minor engaging in sexual acts with St. Pierre.

“Thanks to the dedication of HSI agents, this predator has been removed from the community and is unable to victimize any more minors while allowing the survivor to begin the healing process,” said HSI Chicago Special Agent in Charge, Matthew Scarpino.

St. Pierre admitted to engaging in sexually explicit conduct with the minor on three separate occasions in Olney.

Homeland Security Investigations and the Richland County Sheriff’s Office contributed to the investigation.  Assistant US Attorney David Sanders prosecuted the case.

title: ELECTION REMINDERS
full_story:
The Illinois State Board of Elections is reminding voters of the correct procedures to ensure their vote-by-mail ballots are submitted in time for the upcoming election.

In a press release Thursday, the board said Illinois voters planning to vote by mail should be mindful of postal service postmarking procedures and ballot return options to make sure their votes are counted in the March 17th primary election.

Under Illinois law, vote-by-mail ballots delivered through the United States Postal Service can only be counted if they are postmarked on or before Election Day and arrive within two weeks after Election Day.

Voters that use the postal service to return their ballots should also be aware that a ballot dropped in a mailbox or handed to a letter carrier will likely not receive a postmark until the mail is processed at a regional facility, which is usually a day or two later.

Any voters returning ballots by mail close to the March 17th primary are advised to visit a postal service retail location and have their ballot manually postmarked.

The board said most of Illinois’ 108 local election authorities also offer secure drop boxes that allow voters to return their ballots without putting them in the mail.

Voters are also able to return their marked mail-in ballots in person to the office of their local election authority.  Anyone wanting to vote by mail will have until March 12th to request a ballot from their local election authority.

title: WEATHER SPOTTER CLASS
full_story:
With spring storm season ahead, the National Weather Service has scheduled a weather spotter training class in Effingham on March 10th.

The course is free and open to anyone, but only people age 18 and older will be considered storm spotters.  Topics covered during the course include severe weather hazards, safety concerns, planning for severe weather, general thunderstorm structure and movement, and how to identify important storm features.  The class will last approximately two hours, according to the NWS.

The NWS said you don’t have to live in the county where the course is being offered to attend.  The class on March 10th will be held at the County Emergency Operations Center, at 311 W Miracle Avenue, and start at 6:30 pm.
